newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka navy says sinks two rebel boats.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka navy says sinks two rebel boats.

text.p: The Sri Lankan navy sank two Tamil Tiger guerrilla boats when it intercepted a rebel flotilla off the northeastern coast of this Indian Ocean island early on Thursday, navy officials said.
At least 15 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels were believed killed in a sea battle that lasted more than three hours, they said.
The rebel boats were on their way to the coastal rebel base of Mullaitivu when they were intercepted by naval gunboats between Pulmoddai and Almapil.
"We believe at least 15 rebels were killed, it could be more," a navy spokesman said.
Three other rebel boats were also heavily damaged and were seen beached off Almapil, he said.
One naval gunboat had been slightly damaged in the battle, which took place about 260 km (160 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo.
The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the war began in 1983.
The LTTE put the toll higher.
